title: Powder B: cation exchange and freeze drying
method_label: Powder B: cation exchange and freeze drying
scopeLabel: Main article only; synthesis route. Named source populations are linked; physical aliquot and cross-technique identity are unknown. The supplied main-article scope and source-bound presentation passed independent review; SI unverified.
summary: Dissolve the stated but unquantified precursor charge in deionized water in an ice bath. The bath temperature is not numerically reported. Slowly add ammonia to the stirred solution until alpha-stannic-acid precipitation is complete. Preserve the prose/Figure 1 formulation ambiguity. Figure 1 branches from precipitated alpha-stannic acid to sodium stannate. No 100 °C drying step is inherited from A and no shared physical batch is asserted. Dilute the sodium stannate solution; final volume is unreported. Add small resin portions, age 15 min after each cycle to approach hydrolytic equilibrium, and monitor pH. The resulting colloid has pH 6.5. No total number of cycles or resin-removal operation is specified. Freeze-dry the colloid to friable powder. The Results discuss liquid-nitrogen freezing as the platelet-template explanation; the operational freezing/drying schedule is not supplied.

conflictPairs.context: Ammonia is called liquid ammonia in the Experimental prose, while Figure 1 labels NH3(aq). The formulation is not resolved and no ammonia concentration is inferred.
Figure 3 calls as-prepared A amorphous; the Figure 5 annealing-time discussion starts from 4 nm. The latter is retained only in its time-series context, not assigned as the as-prepared SEM/XRD size.
The 600 °C time series is distinct from the 24 h temperature series; no temperatures or time ticks are converted to invented individual tabulated measurements.
Source calls its microscopy SEM and names 2000FX JEOL. The method/instrument wording is retained without silently substituting TEM.
The 50 µm agglomerate size and resistance unit Ω are visually read from the printed page; cached OCR misreads these as mm and V.
Text summarizes A as 20 nm at 60 h, whereas the two Figure 5 reflection traces differ visually. Textual 20 nm is not a precise value for both reflections.
Text gives approximately 70 m²/g at 300 °C for both populations. Figure 7 B is visually higher; no plot-derived replacement is made.
Figure 4 axis says mass loss (%) while curves descend from 100. Only the explicit text water-loss values are extracted; the axis is not repaired.

unresolved: Independent scientific and Reader audit pending. This is an author draft, not admission or publication.
Physical aliquot IDs and SEM/XRD/TG/Auger crosswalk are not reported; links use the named A/B preparation population only.
No atomic coordinates, complete lattice constants, measured particle-size distribution or gas-sensing response is provided.
Heating/cooling ramps and specimen masses are unreported. Cited separate cryosol methods were not read to fill gaps.
SnCl4·5H2O mass, water volume, initial concentration, ammonia amount/concentration/addition duration, stirring rate, centrifuge force/time, wash volumes/count and yield are unreported.

Figure 1 shares the precipitated alpha-stannic-acid precursor. The body explicitly gives centrifugation/washing for A; their repetition before the B stannate step is not separately stated and is not encoded as a B operation.

Alpha-stannic-acid charge, NaOH volume, total stannate volume, resin identity/capacity/total mass/cycle count/separation are unreported. Freeze-drying pressure, duration, exact freezing time/rate and full schedule are absent.

general_background.title: Changing cations in an existing solid
general_background.summary: Cation exchange changes the cation population of an existing material while transport and interface motion govern the transformation. Retention of an anion framework or particle shape depends on the particular system.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
